prompt:
Add and export `isExpiringSoon(item, now, days = 3)` in src/expiry.js: true when the item has not expired and expires within `days` days (use `daysLeft`). Then make `GET /expiring` use it and accept `?days=N` (default 7, so the current behavior stays). `days` must be a whole number from 0 to 365; anything else answers status 400. `handle(path, now)` receives the path with its query string.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added `isExpiringSoon(item, now, days = 3)` in src/expiry.js and made `GET /expiring` use it. The route takes `?days=N` (default 7) and answers 400 `invalid_days` for anything that isn't a whole number from 0 to 365. `npm test` (7/7) and lint pass. I also ran a manual check: no `days` still returns only milk, and bad values like 366, -1, 1.5, an empty value and abc all get 400. Other changes: `handle` now reads the path and query itself, the server passes it the full `req.url`, and the README route list and CHANGELOG are updated. One difference: the function works from `daysLeft` alone, so `/expiring` no longer logs the "item expired" warning that `isExpired` used to write.
